The repo's demos/painter_cells/main.cpp has a benchmark mode (num_frames, num_skip_frames, per-frame times), but the Qt, Cairo and Skia ports, GPU model, driver and build flags are not public here, so C is the cap.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Snippet only (XDC 2016 slides on x.org, egress-blocked, not opened). painter-cells frame rate normalized to Cairo's CPU renderer (1.00): at 600 cells FastUIDraw 9.33, Skia GL 1.91, Cairo Xlib 1.60, Qt Raster 1.01, Qt GL 0.76, Qt Native 0.29, Cairo GL 0.27; at 1250 cells FastUIDraw 11.11, Qt Raster 1.50, Skia GL 1.36, Cairo Xlib 1.25, Qt GL 0.45, Cairo GL 0.15, Qt Native 0.14. Against Skia's GL backend that is about 4.9x at 600 cells, 8.2x at 1250 cells and 5.5x in the abstract's set (derived from snippet data); the 9x figure is against Cairo's CPU renderer.
corrections.workload: painter-cells demo (demos/painter_cells in the repo): a table of cells, each with a background, a rotating and moving image and a rotating and moving line of text clipped to the cell, with anti-aliased stroked cell boundaries; the author ported it to Qt (Raster, GL, Native), Cairo (CPU, GL, Xlib) and Skia GL and compared frame rates at 600 and 1250 cells, normalized to Cairo CPU.
corrections.hardware: Unnamed laptop with an Intel GPU, described as 3+ years old in 2016 (search snippet of the blocked XDC 2016 abstract page); GPU model, driver, OS and build flags not given.
corrections.caveats: Snippet only: the numbers come from search-result text of Kevin Rogovin's XDC 2016 slides (x.org/wiki/Events/XDC2016/Program/fast_ui_draw.pdf) and the XDC 2016 abstract page; x.org, Phoronix, mail-archive (webkit-dev thread) and the Chromium graphics-dev post are all egress-blocked here, so nothing was read in full. First-party, single clipping-heavy demo, ten years old (Skia, Cairo and Qt of 2016). The repo's demos/painter_cells has a benchmark mode (num_frames, num_skip_frames), but the Qt, Cairo and Skia ports used for comparison are not in the repo or in the author's public forks (krogueintel lists skia.fastuidraw and qtwebkit.fastuidraw forks with no painter-cells code shown). The headline 9x compares GPU rendering against Cairo's CPU renderer; against Skia GL the win is about 4.9x to 8.2x depending on cell count (derived from snippet data). A search summary of a Hacker News thread says the benchmarks were not representative. Intel archived the repository on 2023-01-07 with a discontinuation notice (no maintenance, bug fixes or patches accepted); the last code commit is 2019-12-20. Requires GL 3.3 or GLES 3.0 and, for non-Porter-Duff blend modes, framebuffer-fetch or fragment-shader-interlock extensions.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Snippet only (arXiv abstract, blocked): an optimizer that rewrites four patterns of sub-optimal Skia command sequences emitted by Google Chrome, each verified correct in the Lean-mechanized muSkia semantics, gives an 18.7% speedup over Skia's most modern GPU backend on 99 Skia programs gathered from the top 100 websites, and takes at most 32 microseconds to optimize. Hardware, GPU model, Skia version and per-program spread were not seen.
corrections.caveats: Snippet only: arXiv 2603.23696, alphaXiv, ResearchGate and the ACM DOI (10.1145/3839471, Proceedings of the ACM on Programming Languages vol. 10, OOPSLA2, October 2026, per search results) are egress-blocked, so only the abstract text from search results was seen; authors per search results are Bhargav Kulkarni, Henry Whiting and Pavel Panchekha (University of Utah). The 18.7% is an aggregate over 99 web-page Skia programs, not a per-scene range, and the optimizer is a rewrite pass in front of Skia rather than a rasterizer, so the speedup comes from removing redundant layers and state changes in Chrome's command streams. No code repository was found: Panchekha's GitHub only has skia and skia-python forks, and a GitHub-scoped WebSearch found nothing. A WebSearch answer summary (not a listed result) names a Zenodo artifact DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21386615; zenodo is blocked, so neither the DOI nor its contents were checked, and has_code stays false until someone opens it. The formal semantics is in Lean; the optimizer's implementation language is unknown.

The independent Wikimedia numbers in the record exist only in a snippet of the blocked MediaWiki page, so C.

corrections.baseline: librsvg (2.45.5 in the resvg 0.8.0 README charts; 2.50 in the MediaWiki snippet) and QtSvg 5.12.3; Inkscape 1.0 and Batik only in the snippet-only MediaWiki table
corrections.claimed_speedup: First-party (resvg 0.8.0 README, 2019): time to render the Elementary OS Icon Theme 5.0 (3417 files): resvg 0.8.0 19 s with the cairo, raqote or skia backend (35 s with qt), librsvg 2.45.5 24 s, QtSvg 5.12.3 30 s, so about 1.26x faster than librsvg (derived from page data). Oxygen Icon Theme 4.12 (4947 files): resvg 0.8.0 175 s (skia) to 205 s (raqote), librsvg 163 s, QtSvg 160 s, so resvg was about 7% to 26% slower than librsvg there (derived from page data); the README attributes this to librsvg's faster blur and its native but incorrect cairo clipping, and notes QtSvg skips filter, clipPath, mask and pattern. Snippet only (MediaWiki 'SVG benchmarks' page, blocked): resvg 0.14.0 1m04.490s CPU time vs librsvg 2.50 1m46.776s, Inkscape 1.0 7m57.465s, Batik 6m51.560s, about 1.66x faster than librsvg and 7.4x faster than Inkscape (derived from snippet data); a second table on that page, per a snippet, gives resvg 150 s, rsvg 2.42.2 242 s, Inkscape 1610 s, Batik 3686 s.
corrections.workload: resvg 0.8.0 README: wall time to render every SVG of the Elementary OS 5.0 icon theme (3417 files) and the Oxygen 4.12 icon theme (4947 files, converted from .svgz) with each library. MediaWiki SVG benchmarks (snippet only): CPU time to render W3C SVG test files at 512 px with each renderer's command-line tool, resvg 0.14.0, 2021.
corrections.caveats: The reachable numbers are first-party, from the resvg 0.8.0 README (2019), with no hardware, OS, compiler, flags or harness stated; resvg 0.8.0 rendered through cairo, Qt, raqote or Google Skia backends, whereas current resvg renders only through tiny-skia, so those timings do not describe today's code. They are mixed: faster than librsvg on simple icons (Elementary) and slower on the blur- and clip-heavy Oxygen theme. From 0.9 on the README compared only resvg's own backends, and since 0.10 it carries no numbers and says comparing SVG renderers is like comparing apples and oranges. The Wikimedia evaluation (independent, 2021, resvg 0.14.0) is snippet only: www.mediawiki.org, phabricator.wikimedia.org and the librsvg GitLab issue 729 are egress-blocked, so its hardware and command lines are unknown; times are whole-suite CLI runs that include process start-up, which also penalizes Batik's JVM. The baselines differ in SVG feature support (resvg-test-suite correctness per the snippet: resvg 0.831, Inkscape 0.745, librsvg 0.662), so faster and more complete are mixed in one figure. Written in Rust with a C API (crates/c-api); not C++. No benches/ directory exists in the current repo. Other resvg-based entries (resvg-js) are already recorded.
